_meta.role: Software Engineer, Embedded Systems, XR, Platforms and Devices

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on experience writing low-level C and C++ across STM32 and Arduino embedded targets, including real-time FreeRTOS task coordination and bare-metal peripheral drivers. Background spans sensor-integrated device firmware, an XR concept build, and systematic debugging of hardware and software integration failures across multi-component robotic systems.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept using AI-based real-time chroma keying without a green screen; produced full claims documentation and BOM.
Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via ADXL345 accelerometers, Raspberry Pi, and HC-05 Bluetooth.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, evaluating and selecting mechanical, PCB, and AI/ML technologies end-to-end.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI (PyQt, Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization; used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with a low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across multi-servo PWM control, interrupt-driven UART commands, and VL53L0X ToF sensing.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ driving five servos, with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors multiplexed over I2C (TCA9548A) for contact-aware grasping.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s voice-to-picked latency.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Distributed dendrite computations across MPI workers on a SLURM-managed cluster; achieved up to 10.49x speedup with 12 processes while characterizing load-imbalance effects causing up to 65% performance degradation.
